{{Quote|Tell Fleet I still think they are heading for Atrivis to smear the army on Mantooine. If they are following standard operating procedures, they'll be moving tomorrow. If Ackbar moves fast and gets to Mantooine first, he can pop 'em as they come out of hyperspace.|[[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Zgorth'sth]]|<ref name="RASB" />}}
Despite being a small [[Sector/Legends|sector]] in the northern [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], the '''Atrivis sector''' and its inhabitants participated in events of galactic and historic significance. From hosting an outpost of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] in [[30,000 BBY]]; to giving birth to the formidable [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]]; to forming part of the most stable Imperial splinter faction, the [[Pentastar Alignment]], between [[6 ABY/Legends|6]] and [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]]; to supporting the [[Empire-in-exile]] in [[137 ABY]]; the Atrivis sector was involved in tumultuous events. Located in the [[New Territories/Legends|New Territories]], the sector was traversed by the [[Braxant Run/Legends|Braxant]] and [[Relgim Run/Legends|Relgim Run]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]], and was home to several native [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]], including the [[Dazouri]], [[Ho'Din/Legends|Ho'Din]], [[Makurth/Legends|Makurth]], [[Shaliz'Na]] and [[Zeffliffl (species)|Zeffliffl]]. Those civilizations, and the immigrants that joined them in the sector, were united by their fierce independence. Full exploration of the sector began in [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000 BBY]] and continued through until [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]]. During that period, several Ho'Din participated in the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace]] and [[Mandalorian Wars]], while Makurth participated in the [[New Sith Wars]].

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the independent attitude of the Atrivis sector's inhabitants manifested in sympathy for the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. The Confederacy employed the notorious [[Iridium Pirates/Legends|Pirates of Iridium]] to raid supply lines, and ran a [[Weapons Research Facility|research factory]] on [[Fest/Legends|Fest]], but was eventually defeated by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Later, the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] saw the sector placed under the control of [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] as part of [[Oversector Outer]]. The sector was home to some of the earliest resistance to the new, autocratic government, although its inhabitants remained disorganized and internally divided in their resistance efforts until the [[Battle on Mantooine/Legends|massacre]] of [[Mantooine/Legends|Mantooine]] led to the establishment of the unified [[Atrivis Resistance Group/Legends|Atrivis Resistance Group]].

For two [[Standard year/Legends|years]], the Empire constructed the Death Star in the sector's [[Horuz system/Legends|Horuz system]], supporting the [[Space station/Legends|battle station's]] construction with forced labor from penal institutions on [[Gree Baaker]], [[Desolation Station/Legends|Desolation Station]], and [[Despayre]]. The Death Star repelled several assaults by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] before using its [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] to [[Destruction of Despayre|shatter]] Despayre, subsequently leaving the sector on a quest to brutally eliminate the Alliance leadership and cow the galaxy into submission. Armed conflict, however, continued in the sector, with altercations at [[Atrivis]], [[Fest/Legends|Fest]] and [[Spefik]] and as part of [[Operation Cobolt]], contributing to the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].

Following the [[Death/Legends|death]] of [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the Atrivis sector was included within the newly-formed Pentastar Alignment, an Imperial splinter faction led by Grand Moff [[Ardus Kaine]]. The Alignment lent forces to [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]], who personally planned an [[Fall of Generis|assault]] against [[Generis/Legends|Generis]] that transpired only eight days prior to his [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]]. The following year, the death of Kaine during a major offensive [[Operation Shadow Hand|Imperial campaign]] precipitated the eventual transition of the sector into [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] control. It remained in Republic hands for only a few years before being conquered by the [[Yuuzhan Vong War|invading]], extra-galactic [[Yuuzhan Vong]] in [[26 ABY/Legends|26 ABY]]. Following their eventual defeat in [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]], the Atrivis sector soon passed back into Imperial territory as part of a newly resurgent [[Fel Empire|Empire]]. It would remain under Imperial control until after the [[Sith–Imperial War]], when it began to support the [[Empire-in-exile]] of deposed Emperor [[Roan Fel]].

==Description==
The Atrivis [[Sector/Legends|sector]] was a relatively small sector of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]],<ref name="RASB" /> located in the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] north in a region known as the [[New Territories/Legends|New Territories]].<ref name="Atlas" /> Its [[Core Worlds/Legends|coreward]] boundary bordered the [[Cademimu sector/Legends|Cademimu sector]], and, moving clockwise, it also bordered the [[Cassander sector/Legends|Cassander]], [[Albarrio sector/Legends|Albarrio]], [[Relgim sector/Legends|Relgim]] and [[Oplovis sector/Legends|Oplovis sectors]].<ref name="Outer Rim Extra">{{SW|url=news/essential-atlas-outer-rim-sectors|text=The Essential Atlas Extra: Outer Rim Sectors|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> Two major [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperspace routes]] passed through the sector: the [[Braxant Run/Legends|Braxant]] and [[Relgim Run/Legends|Relgim Runs]]. The Braxant Run was the most important route in the entire northern quadrant of the galaxy, beginning at an intersection with the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]]. The Braxant entered the Atrivis sector from [[Ketaris/Legends|Ketaris]] in the Oplovis sector and traversed the [[Fedje system/Legends|Fedje]] and [[Vuchelle system/Legends|Vuchelle systems]] before leaving Atrivis for the Cassander sector. The Relgim Rum began at the [[Fedje]] [[Star system/Legends|system]], but struck out almost perpendicular to the Braxant Run, working its way through a string of Atrivis systems, with a sharp kink west at the [[Nam'ta system/Legends|Nam'ta system]] before continuing across Atrivis and into its namesake, the Relgim sector. By [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], the average population of the sector was less than 1 million per inhabited [[Planet/Legends|planet]], with the exception of Fedje and areas around [[Moltok/Legends|Moltok]], which averaged between 1 and 10 million inhabitants.<ref name="Atlas" />

===Braxant Run star systems===
The planet Fedje, at the intersection of the Braxant and Relgim Runs,<ref name="Atlas" /> was a [[Tree/Legends|forested]] world, home to many exotic arboreal life forms; these included the rare [[folded ear boosqueak]].<ref name="SWR" /> [[Human/Legends|Humans]] settled Fedje, becoming known for the expansive hand gestures that accompanied their oratory.<ref name="VF">''[[Vision of the Future]]''</ref> Located further down the Braxant was [[Vuchelle]], an orange planet<ref name="Hnn" /> right on the three-way border with the Cademimu and Cassander sectors.<ref name="Atlas" />

===Relgim Run star systems===
The [[Fest system/Legends|Fest system]] was a prominent system along the Relgim Run. It contained the planet [[Fest/Legends|Fest]], an urbanized and densely populated world with little remaining wilderness areas. It was equipped with [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]], [[Spy/Legends|spy]] [[Satellite/Legends|satellites]], and an [[Orbit/Legends|orbital]] [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] base. Fest had a history of petty bickering with [[Mantooine/Legends|Mantooine]], another Atrivis sector planet.<ref name="RASB" /> Further along the Relgim Run was the [[Devon system/Legends|Devon system]].<ref name="Atlas" /> Members of a religious sect inhabited its fourth planet, [[Devon Four]].<ref name="CD">''[[The Cestus Deception]]''</ref>

[[File:AtrivisSector.jpg|left|thumb|Selected star systems in the Atrivis sector]]
The [[Generis system/Legends|Generis system]] was located further down the Relgim Run;<ref name="Atlas" /> it contained the planets [[Atrivis 7]],<ref name="CD" /> [[Atrivis]],<ref name="GFT" /> and [[Generis/Legends|Generis]]. Generis was a world of striking natural beauty, covered with rough terrain and lush jungles. The planet had no major settlements, and was only lightly settled.<ref name="TTSB" /> Some of its locals&mdash;a mix of Humans and other [[Species/Legends|species]]&mdash;established wilderness ranches, attracting wealthy offworlders with opportunities to hunt, hike, and raft down white-[[Water/Legends|water]] rapids.<ref name="MF">[[Millennium Falcon (novel)|''Millennium Falcon'']]</ref> The planet was also dotted with ruins<ref name="RASB" /> of the ancient [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] civilization.<ref name="Atlas" /> Atrivis 7 was also inhabited by Humans, who worked as [[Farm/Legends|farmers]] and ranchers.<ref name="CD" />

Continuing along the Relgim Run led to the [[Markbee's Star system/Legends|Markbee's Star system]], containing the [[Water/Legends|water]] world [[Zeffliffl]]. In the [[Salt/Legends|salty]] [[Ocean/Legends|seas]] of its southern continent, the [[Zeffliffl (species)|Zeffliffl]] species evolved.<ref name="CS">''[[The Crystal Star]]''</ref> After Zeffliffl, the Relgim Run continued onto the Nam'ta system. It was there,<ref name="Atlas" /> in the system containing the [[Gas giant/Legends|gas giant]] [[Nam'ta]],<ref name="SWR" /> that the Run kinked westward, continuing on towards the [[Horuz system/Legends|Horuz system]].<ref name="Atlas" /> The Horuz system contained the planet [[Despayre]], two gas giants and two [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] [[Asteroid field/Legends|belts]]. Despayre's single continent was covered in dense jungle filled with diverse [[Poison/Legends|poisonous]] species such as the [[crab spider]], [[flit]] and [[scorpion slug]]. Because of these attributes, the planet was turned into a [[Prison/Legends|prison]] for many of the worst criminal offenders in the galaxy.<ref name="DS" />

The [[Mantooine system/Legends|Mantooine system]] was located on the Relgim Run near to its crossover into the Relgim sector.<ref name="Atlas" /> The planet Mantooine was only lightly populated with farmers and had a long-standing rivalry with Fest.<ref name="RASB" /> It lent its name to the classical dance piece known as the ''[[Mantooine Minuet]]''.<ref name="Mara">''[[Star Wars: Mara Jade – By the Emperor's Hand]]''</ref> It was also the endpoint of cruises by the giant [[Luxury liner/Legends|luxury liner]] [[Kuari Princess/Legends|''Kuari Princess'']], which traveled down the Relgim Run between [[Endoraan]] and Mantooine.<ref name="SWAJ" />

===Other star systems===
The Atrivis sector had a number of other star systems that were not located on either of the two most prominent routes. The [[Hethar system/Legends|Hethar system]] was located on the eastern border of the sector.<ref name="Atlas" /> Native to [[Hethar]] was the [[Gornt/Legends|gornt]] species. These squat creatures were a staple of the local diet and were later commercially farmed by [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] colonists and sold to the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]].<ref name="CotG" />

Further west in the sector were the [[Iridium system/Legends|Iridium]], [[Gibbela system/Legends|Gibbela]], [[Spefik system/Legends|Spefik]] and [[Dartibek system]]s.<ref name="Atlas" /> [[Iridium]] was home for a time to the [[Iridium Pirates/Legends|Pirates of Iridium]],<ref name="Hnn" /> while [[Gibbela]]&mdash;close to the Relgim border<ref name="Atlas" />&mdash;was populated by a primitive species of polymorphs, known as the [[Dazouri]].<ref name="Hiding" /> It was distant from even minor trade routes, and was seldom visited.<ref name="Tales" /> The Spefik system was home to [[Spefik]], a desolate and barren planet. During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], it hosted a [[Spefik base|Rebel base]].<ref name="RoC" />

[[File:Desolation_Station.jpg|thumb|right|Desolation Station]]
The Dartibek system was at the western-most extent of the Atrivis sector, at the joining of the Atrivis, Albarrio and Relgim sectors.<ref name="Atlas" /> The system contained a number of planets; one of the innermost was Moltok, which was entirely covered in trees. Although close to its [[Star/Legends|sun]], the planet was kept temperate by ash from [[Volcano/Legends|volcanoes]] that blocked out [[Radiation/Legends|radiation]] and heat. Its botanical species included the [[wuppa]]<ref name="GG4">''[[Galaxy Guide 4: Alien Races]]''</ref> and [[Camba-Fruit]]; derivatives of the latter were commercially exported.<ref name="CoJ">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref> Moltok was home to two [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] species: the [[Ho'Din/Legends|Ho'Din]]<ref name="GG4" /> and the [[Makurth/Legends|Makurth]].<ref name="CCG">{{CCG|set=Special Edition Limited|cardname=Makurth}}</ref>

The Atrivis sector also contained the [[Gree Baaker system/Legends|Gree Baaker system]].<ref name="TEAOC" /> Its eponymous [[Gree Baaker|planet]] was home to an Imperial [[Gree Baaker Labor Camp|Labor Camp]] for those serving life sentences.<ref name="Target">''[[Rebel Force: Target]]''</ref> Also located within the sector was a [[Desolation Station system|system]] that contained an asteroid belt. Built within a large, misshaped asteroid in this system was [[Desolation Station/Legends|Desolation Station]], an Imperial construction facility that utilized [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] labor.<ref name="Elite" /> Finally, the sector contained the [[Shar'Ack system/Legends|Shar'Ack system]].<ref name="TEAOC" />

==History==
===Pre-Republic history===
{{Quote|Long ago the Rakata ruled all the known galaxy; all species bowed down to us.|The Rakata [[Orsaa]]|<ref name="SWKOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
In [[30,000 BBY]], the planet Generis possessed a strong [[The Force/Legends|Force]] signature. As a consequence, it attracted the Force-based [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrives]] of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] species who were expanding from their homeworld [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]]. The Rakata forged a vast empire that united worlds scattered all across the galaxy, naming it the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]].<ref name="Atlas" /> On Generis, they built exotic temples that would last for thousands of [[Standard year/Legends|years]].<ref name="RASB" /> The Rakatan empire lasted for almost five thousand years before collapsing due to [[plague]], followed by slave revolts in [[25,200 BBY]].<ref name="Atlas" /> Their temples on Generis eventually collapsed and were overgrown by jungle.<ref name="RASB" />

===Galactic Republic===
====Early exploration====
{{Quote|In addition to the already-reported promotion of Saul Karath of the ''Courageous'' to Rear Admiral, the latest promotions were handed down from the Republic Navy &hellip; To Lieutenant: &hellip; Rutu of Moltok.|The Admiral's List|<ref name="Admiral's List">{{KOTORbackups|13}}</ref>}}
[[File:Atrivis-MandoWar.jpg|thumb|left|The Atrivis sector was connected to the Republic by a hyperlane, which was attacked during the Mandalorian Wars.]]
Some systems within the Atrivis sector were discovered by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during the [[Kymoodon Era]], circa [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000 BBY]]. New advances in [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] technology at this time led to exploration of pockets of space not directly connected with the territory of the Republic; in the north these included the Mantooine and [[Sestooine system/Legends|Sestooine systems]] (the latter would become part of the Relgim sector), and spread to include the Dartibek and Horuz systems.<ref name="Atlas" />

During the [[Pius Dea Era]] of [[11,965 BBY|11,965]]-[[10,966 BBY]], the Atrivis sector suffered suppression by the [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]-based religious sect [[Pius Dea]]. Hoping to escape Pius Dea rule, Republic citizens abandoned [[Fedje]] and settled the [[Prefsbelt system/Legends|Prefsbelt system]].<ref name="Warfare121">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

By [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], the Dartibek system&mdash;which contained the planet Moltok&mdash;and other parts of the Atrivis sector were widely explored by the Republic and were considered part of the civilized galaxy. The Republic had also established a [[Coruscant–Dantooine hyperlane|hyperlane]] connecting Moltok to the central territories of the Republic via [[Ord Cantrell/Legends|Ord Cantrell]], [[Iridonia/Legends|Iridonia]] and [[Vicondor/Legends|Vicondor]].<ref name="Atlas" /> The Ho'Din of Moltok had traveled offworld by this time; during the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]], [[Lohjoy]] served as a [[Starship/Legends|starship]] [[Engineer/Legends|engineer]] aboard the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] starship ''[[Omen]]''.<ref name="Precipice">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Precipice]]''</ref>

A number of Ho'Din also served the Republic in [[3964 BBY]], such as [[Oojoh]]<ref name="Commencement">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic: Commencement]]''</ref> and [[Rutu]].<ref name="Admiral's List" /> Oojoh was trained as a [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] on [[Taris/Legends|Taris]],<ref name="Commencement" /> while [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] Rutu served with distinction in the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] during the [[Mandalorian Wars]].<ref name="Admiral's List" /> The extent of the widely explored area around Moltok remained largely static through this period until at least [[3956 BBY]].<ref name="Atlas" />

Between [[3681 BBY]] and [[3653 BBY]], the [[Great Galactic War]] pitted the forces of the Galactic Republic against the resurgent forces of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]].<ref name="SW:TOR" /> As a side event of that campaign, the Republic was involved in the [[Kanz Disorders/Legends|Kanz Disorders]] of [[3670 BBY]], after which the Republic shrunk its borders to Iridonia in the north, and began reconsidering Republic membership for distant settlements and Republic enclaves.<ref name="Atlas" /> After a significant victory at [[Sacking of Coruscant|Coruscant]], the Sith forced the Republic to sign the [[Treaty of Coruscant]], which effectively divided the galaxy into two spheres of control. The Atrivis sector fell within the sphere of control of the Sith Empire, which compromised most of the eastern half of the galaxy. Despite the signing of the peace treaty, relations were uneasy between the galactic powers: a [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] lasted for over a decade years, before [[Galactic War|outright war]] returned in [[3641 BBY]].<ref name="Date3641">{{TOR_dates|3}}</ref> Around that time, an [[Unidentified organization (Nam'ta)|independent organization]] on the planet Nam'ta claimed to have received thousands of diplomatic dispatches from the Galactic Republic. Its plan to release these onto the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] was uncovered, and pressure brought to bear on the [[Nam'ta government]] to clamp down on the organization.<ref name="SWTOR">{{TORcite|type=crewskill|Diplomacy|Stopping the Leaks}}</ref>

====Later exploration====
{{Quote|My younger sister joined a religious sect on Devon Four. When they refused to pay taxes Coruscant slapped an embargo on them. When a plague struck the colony, they were going to die, every woman, man, and child. No one would do a thing.|Sheeka Tull|<ref name="CD" />}}
[[File:Atrivis_exploration.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Exploration of the Atrivis sector and surrounding territories]]
The eastern portion of the Atrivis sector was not fully explored until the blazing of the Hydian Way, circa [[3000 BBY|3000]]&ndash;[[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]].<ref name="Atlas" /> The Makurth, the second sentient species of Moltok, were found off-world by at least 1000 BBY; during the [[New Sith Wars]], the Makurth [[Fohargh]] underwent [[Sith training|training]] as part of the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]],<ref name="Bane">''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]''</ref> although Moltok itself was unaligned in the conflict.<ref name="Atlas" /> [[300 BBY/Legends|Seven hundred years]] later, the Ho'Din almost destroyed the ecosystem of their planet, leading them to embrace botanical sciences and other less invasive disciplines in restoring their world. By [[280 BBY/Legends|280 BBY]], they had developed organic medicines that came to be exported around the galaxy.<ref name="EGtAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> Another Ho'Din product available offworld was [[Ho'Din herbal tea]]; some combinations proved addictive to Humans.<ref name="CRO">''[[Cracken's Rebel Operatives]]''</ref>

In [[124 BBY]], the Atrivis sector, together with the rest of the Outer Rim and parts of the Mid Rim, was declared by the Galactic Republic to be a free-trade zone. However, in the [[30 BBY/Legends|30s]], a political faction known as the [[Reformist]]s sought to roll back that liberalization, and place taxes on many Rim trade routes.<ref name="Warfare 49">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> Several years before the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] would embroil the galaxy, the religious leaders of Devon Four refused to pay taxes to the central galactic government. In response, the Republic embargoed the planet, preventing any starship traffic from reaching its surface. Shortly after the embargo was initiated, an infectious plague broke out on the planet's surface. Despite the threat this posed to the planet's population, the Republic was unrelenting in its embargo. At the behest of [[Sheeka Tull]], whose [[Sheeka Tull's sister|sister]] lived on Devon Four, [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] broke the Republic embargo, delivering medical supplies. Sheeka Tull was later caught by the Republic and was given a deferred sentence of ten years labor.<ref name="CD" />

====The Clone Wars====
{{Quote|ATRIVIS SECTOR NODE - Sensor reports from the Atrivis sector issued by the Judicial Department confirm that a Jedi task force has thrashed the space pirates of Iridium, bringing an end to their year-long raids along the Atrivis sector routes.|"Jedi Smash Iridium Pirates; 3 Knights Killed" news item|<ref name="Hnn" />}}
During the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], circa [[24 BBY/Legends|24]]&ndash;[[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] hired the Pirates of Iridium as [[Privateer/Legends|privateers]]. The [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] had been active in the Atrivis sector for a [[Standard year/Legends|year]], raiding its trade routes.<ref name="Hnn" /> They were distinguished by their use of [[power gem]]s. These unusual jewels radiated an aura that disrupted starships' [[Deflector shield/Legends|magnetic-shields]], an ability the pirates used to great advantage during their raids.<ref name="Power">"[[The Power Gem]]"</ref> During the Separatist Crisis, they raided Republic grain and [[Spice/Legends|spice]] convoys until they were destroyed in 22 BBY by a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]-led Republic strike force at a [[skirmish over Vuchelle]].<ref name="Hnn" />

When the Clone Wars finally broke out, the Atrivis sector was part of Confederate territory.<ref name="Atlas" /> Less than ten [[Standard month/Legends|months]] into the war, they had established a [[Separatist Phrik factory|research factory]] on Fest in which they were developing a super-metal known as [[Phrik/Legends|phrik]]. The facility was discovered by [[Null-class Advanced Recon Commando]]s, and [[21 BBY/Legends|ten months]] into the war, the Republic dispatched the elite [[Omega Squad]] to [[Raid on Fest|destroy]] the factory. Encountering heavy resistance from [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]], they nevertheless successfully completed the mission.<ref name="Republic Commando" /> By [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the Republic had successfully recovered control of the Atrivis sector.<ref name="Atlas" />

===Galactic Empire===
====Early resistance====
{{Quote|The Empire is making its presence felt more and more out here in the Rim. There was that massacre on that humanoid-inhabited world&hellip;''"<br />"''Mantooine in the Atrivis Sector.|[[Jiliac Desilijic Tiron]] and [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]|<ref name="RD" />}}
With the [[Declaration of a New Order|declaration]] of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]] in 19 BBY, the Atrivis sector came under control of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. The sector fell under the jurisdiction of [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Tarkin]] as part of [[Oversector Outer]].<ref name="DS" /> Oversectors such as this one were created to encompass numerous sectors known to house chronic unrest or rebellion, and facilitate swift Imperial retribution across sector boundaries.<ref name="DSTC">''[[Death Star Technical Companion]]''</ref> [[Moff/Legends|Moffs]] [[Rebus (Galactic Empire)|Rebus]]<ref name="DF" /> and [[Kohl Seerdon|Seerdon]] also had projects within the sector.<ref name="RS" /> The Atrivis sector was at the forefront of opposition to the New Order, due in large part to the stubborn independence common throughout much of the Outer Rim Territories. However, in its early years, the sector's resistance was fractured and lacking unity, with resistance groups scattered across many systems and divided by regional and historic rivalries. Nonetheless, this continued annoyance prompted the Empire to establish a [[garrison]] post on Mantooine to keep order in the sector.<ref name="RASB" />

[[File:Travia_chan.jpg|thumb|left|Travia Chan, founder of the Fest Resistance Group]]
In [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]],<ref name="time">This battle was known of in ''[[Rebel Dawn]]'', which takes place in 2 BBY.</ref> the [[Mantooine Liberators]] resistance group [[Battle on Mantooine/Legends|overthrew]] this under-defended garrison and boldly occupied the premises. The Liberators were unaware of a large Imperial strike force in the neighboring Fest system, and had no contact with the Fest resistance group that could have warned them of this danger. As such, the Mantooine resistance was caught by surprise when Imperial forces arrived in Mantooine; the local rebels were decimated.<ref name="RASB" /> There were also extensive civilian casualties in the battle,<ref name="Atlas" /> which as heard of as far afield as [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]] and came to be regarded as a massacre.<ref name="RD" /> The Rebel Alliance honored the sacrifice of those who lost their lives on Mantooine by casting the [[Mantooine Medallion/Legends|Mantooine Medallion]], which was awarded to individuals for "exceptionally meritorious service."<ref name="SW:XW">[[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']]</ref> Years later, a [[CR90 corvette/Legends|Corellian Corvette]] was named the [[Mantooine (CR90 corvette)|''Mantooine'']] in honor of the planet.<ref name="IR">''[[X-Wing: Isard's Revenge]]''</ref>

The massacre on Mantooine drove home the necessity of communication to the other resistance groups in the Atrivis sector; the [[Fest Resistance Group]] responded by forming a wider [[Atrivis Resistance Group/Legends|Atrivis Resistance Group]] (ARG) to coordinate resources within the sector. The ARG established a hidden base on an abandoned [[Space station/Legends|space station]] in the barren Generis system, where their leadership was fed information from an extensive network across the sector. This centralization made the resistance a significantly more potent force, although their continuing success also brought concerns; they were still isolated within their system and vulnerable to Imperial offensives launched from outside the sector.<ref name="RASB" />

[[File:Gibbela_transforms.jpg|right|thumb|An Imperial mission to the planet Gibbela went badly awry.]]
Elsewhere in the sector, the Empire established a Labor Camp on Gree Baaker, where many individuals were sentenced to life imprisonment.<ref name="Target" /> The Empire scouted Gibbela as a possible site for colonization, with preliminary reconnaissance suggesting the native population would provide little resistance;<ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> however, when a small taskforce was [[Mission to Gibbela|dispatched]] to the planet, it was massacred by [[Unidentified Dazouri farmer|one]] such native after he polymorphed into a vicious predator.<ref name="Tales" />

====The Death Star====
{{Quote|The Death Star is a fearsome invention indeed. We must find a way to destroy it!|Rahm Kota|<ref name="Elite" />}}
During this period, a crucial Imperial project was under construction in the Atrivis sector: the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]]. This immense [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]], designed with the capacity to destroy planets, was to be the foundation of the [[Tarkin Doctrine/Legends|Tarkin Doctrine]],<ref name="DS" /> whereby the Empire would "rule through the fear of force rather than through force itself."<ref name="DSTC" /> After initial construction phases in the [[Geonosis system/Legends|Geonosis]], [[Seswenna system/Legends|Seswenna]], and [[Patriim system/Legends|Patriim systems]], the construction was finally moved to the Horuz system for completion.<ref name="Atlas" />

There, it orbited the penal world Despayre for two years. The system's two [[Asteroid field/Legends|asteroid belts]]<ref name="DS" /> were stripped of [[Iron/Legends|iron]] and [[nickel]] by Imperial [[masticator]]s, and combined with alloys obtained from Despayre. The planet's [[Moon/Legends|moon]], [[Haroon]], was also [[Mining/Legends|mined]] for resources. Construction utilized convict labor, in particular, that of thousands of [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]].<ref name="Atlas" /> Prisoners from the Gree Baaker Labor Camp were also assigned to work duty on the station.<ref name="Target" /> The Empire also utilized Desolation Station to manufacture several components of its [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]]<ref name="Elite" /> with which the Death Star would be able to rupture the core of planets, ultimately shattering its targets into pieces.<ref name="Star Wars">{{Film|IV}}</ref> The construction of the station was kept top secret.<ref name="Elite" />

[[File:PalpatineGalenduel.jpg|thumb|left|Emperor Palpatine and Galen Marek fought aboard the Death Star.]]
Emperor Palpatine himself visited the Death Star while it was under construction in the Horuz system, for the culmination of his strategy to crush organized leadership of resistance to his Empire. Imprisoned aboard the station were four critical leaders of rebellion: three influential senators [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]] of [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] of [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]] and [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], together with Jedi Master and [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]]-survivor [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]]. The four leaders had met on Corellia and formally [[Corellian Treaty|declared]] an [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|organized rebellion]] against the Empire. However, the four had actually been manipulated to meet on Corellia by Imperial machinations implemented by [[Galen Marek]], a pupil of the Emperor's apprentice [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]; they were captured and transferred to the Death Star for interrogation.<ref name="TFU" />

Marek, however, had earnestly believed his efforts to draw together the insurrectionists would lead to the overthrow of the Emperor. Marek was furious at being duped. Uncovering the location of the Death Star in a [[Farsight/Legends|Force vision]], he traveled to the Atrivis sector and [[Battle on Death Star I|infiltrated]] the vast construction site. Having inciting Wookiee slave laborers to riot, two of the laborers guided Marek to the Emperor's location. There, Marek dueled and defeated Darth Vader; before ultimately engaging the Emperor in direct combat. This provided a sufficient diversion for the four captives to flee the battle station to safety, although Marek perished in encounter.<ref name="TFU" />

====Formalizing Rebellion====
Senator Mon Mothma would return to the Atrivis sector, where she met with the leadership of the Atrivis Resistance Group. She proposed linking the ARG into the newly established Rebellion. After some deliberation, the ARG signed the [[Treaty of Generis]], officially joining the Rebel Alliance for the duration of the Galactic Civil War. As part of this deal, an [[Outer Rim Communications Center]] was established on Generis, with a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] outpost to protect it. The Alliance also sent several dozen [[Alliance Special Forces/Legends|SpecForce]] officers to train up the Atrivis resistance. The Treaty also meant a flow of new weapons and equipment to the sector, in return for becoming a prime supplier of foodstuffs to the wider Rebellion. Within six months, the ARG transformed into a fully operational [[Atrivis Sector Force]].<ref name="RASB" /> Rebel units that operated within Atrivis sector included the [[132nd Forward Division]].<ref name="MTSB">''[[Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition]]''</ref>

[[File:Desolation_Station_destroyed.jpg|thumb|right|The Rebel Alliance destroyed Desolation Station.]]
Kota subsequently directed several efforts to undermine the completion of the Death Star. He [[Mission to Desolation Station|dispatched]] former-Imperial stormtrooper [[X2]] to Desolation Station to prevent one of the final components of the superlaser&mdash;the [[tributary beam]]&mdash;from being delivered to the Death Star. As the tributary beam was being stored on a transport that was protected by a defensive shield corridor, X2 was required to infiltrate the facility and deactivate the shield. Prior to deactivating the shields, X2 released some [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] laborers held on the station. With their help, X2 fled the station aboard a captured [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighter]] and, with cover provided by Rebel starfighter reinforcements, managed to infiltrate and gain control of the tributary-carrying transport. X2 activated the beam, using it to destroy Desolation Station. This mission set back the construction timetable of the Death Star.<ref name="Elite" />

Following this sabotage, the Alliance undertook an audacious [[Mission to Death Star I|reconnaissance mission]] to the site of the Death Star itself. Starfighters under the direction of Master Kota entered the Horuz system and engaged enemy starfighters. X2, a volunteer on this mission, was able to infiltrate a supporting ''Imperial''-class [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]], using its weapons emplacements to strike at the Death Star.<ref name="Elite" />

This and other damage inflicted on the Death Star provided a small opportunity for some Rebels on board the station itself. While some set about freeing prisoners aboard the station, X2 used the partially completed superlaser to strike at the Star Destroyer he had only recently departed, destroying it completely. Having glimpsed the destructive potential of the battlestation, the Rebel strike team extracted themselves from the battle and fled the Horuz system to deliver their intelligence to [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]].<ref name="Elite" />

Following this strike, the Alliance launched a more substantial [[Attack on the first Death Star|assault]] on the station, led by the ''[[Fortressa]]'', a [[Lucrehulk-class LH-3210 cargo freighter/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class]] starfighter carrier. Launching at least 500 starfighters, the assault was a disastrous failure, with the ''Fortressa'' destroyed early by a low powered beam from the Death Star and its fighters soon picked off by supporting Imperial forces.<ref name="DS" />

[[File:Destruction_of_Despayre-TEA.jpg|thumb|left|The Death Star destroyed the planet Despayre.]]
Despite these attempts by the resistance to slow completion of the Death Star, the battlestation was finished soon after. Before departing the sector for the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], the station's [[Concave Dish Composite Beam Superlaser|superlaser]] was [[Destruction of Despayre|tested]] on Despayre; in three successive blasts, the prison world was destroyed, eliminating all inhabitants.<ref name="DS" /> [[Rianna Saren]], an escapee from the prison world below who had infiltrated the station only shortly before this destruction, contacted [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], a high-ranking member of the Rebellion and daughter of Bail Organa, from the station and informed her of Despayre's destruction as well as the location of schematics of the Death Star located on the planet [[Danuta]]. Saren then fled the station to Danuta, part of a multi-pronged attempt to [[Operation Skyhook|secure the plans]] to the Death Star.<ref name="Lethal">''[[Star Wars: Lethal Alliance]]''</ref>

Following this destruction, the battlestation left the sector; however, the Empire left some forces in the system in case any members of the Alliance came to investigate. Shortly after, two [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvettes]] collectively compromising ''[[Ethar]]'' was dispatched to the system and [[Skirmish in the Horuz system|captured]] by the Imperial forces. Further Alliance forces arrived in the system shortly after, and starfighters from [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red Squadron]], [[Blue Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Blue Squadron]] and [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Gold Squadron]] managed to recover the corvettes.<ref name="XWOSG" />

The Death Star itself traveled to Alderaan in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], where its destructive power was publicly demonstrated with the [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destruction]] of that planet. It then traveled to the [[Yavin system/Legends|Yavin system]], intending to destroy the leadership of the Rebel Alliance. In a [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|climactic battle]], however, the Death Star was destroyed. Grand Moff Tarkin perished along with his battlestation<ref name="Star Wars" /> and control of Oversector Outer&mdash;and, consequently, the Atrivis sector&mdash;passed to Grand Moff [[Ardus Kaine]],<ref name="Atlas" /> a brilliant theorist and strategist known for his emphasis on success through total domination.<ref name="Pentastar">{{JournalCite|3|The Pentastar Alignment}}</ref>

====Further conflict====
{{Quote|&mdash;you shoulda' seen the results of our tests on Fest&mdash;my weapons are gonna put a lot of holes in a lot of Rebel scum.|Moff Rebus under interrogation|<ref name="DF" />}}
Despite the significant blow dealt to the Empire at the Battle of Yavin, its control of the Atrivis sector continued. As part of another Imperial project in the Atrivis sector, the Empire re-established phrik processing on Fest. The alloy phrik was then used in the [[Dark Trooper Project]], producing extremely strong, lightweight [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[Armor/Legends|armor]]. Shortly after the Battle of Yavin, the [[Dark Trooper/Legends|Dark troopers]] were [[Attack on Tak Base|tested]] against a [[Tak Base|Rebel base]] on [[Talay/Legends|Talay]]. Upon investigating, Rebel operative [[Kyle Katarn]] tracked the source of the attack to Moff Rebus, in charge of the project. Rebus revealed the phrik was being processed at the Imperial [[Weapons Research Facility]] on Fest. Traveling to the planet, Katarn [[Mission to Fest (Galactic Civil War)|infiltrated]] the Imperial operation, stealing a sample of phrik. The sample led Katarn to the source of [[phrikite]] on [[Gromas 16]], and eventually led to the derailing of the Dark Trooper Project.<ref name="DF" />

[[File:C3l2.jpg|thumb|right|Rebels stole three All Terrain Personal Transports on Fest.]]
Further action occurred on Fest in [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], when Rebel resistance again [[Escape from Fest|raided]] the Weapons Research Facility in order to steal three [[All Terrain Personal Transport/Legends|All Terrain Personal Transports]]. While the Rebels initially broke the transports out from the Imperial facility, they required aerial cover from [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] to make good their escape. The successful raid upset Imperial Moff Kohl Seerdon, who was in charge of the research, and in retaliation the Moff [[Blockade on Chandrila|blockaded]] [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]], homeworld of Rebel leader Mon Mothma.<ref name="RS" />

While these successes were significant for the Alliance, they also suffered various defeats at the hands of the Empire. An Imperial force of at least two [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighter]] [[Fighter wing/Legends|wings]] [[Battle of Spefik|attacked]] their base on the planet Spefik. According to reports, elite pilot [[Ranulf Trommer/Legends|Ranulf Trommer]] single-handedly destroyed the Rebel's anti-orbital [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannons]] defending the base.<ref name="RoC" /> The elite [[Storm commando/Legends|Storm commandos]] were also deployed in the sector on [[Atrivis]] where the rebel [[X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]] pilot [[Homack]] was shot down.<ref name="GFT" /> Other Imperial counter-measures included spraying toxic defoliants across many worlds of the sector in an effort to cripple the agricultural capacity of the sector's resistance.<ref name="RASB" />

Sometime after 1 ABY,<ref name="Madine">This timeline placement is based on the involvement of [[Crix Madine/Legends|Crix Madine]] in planning the mission. He did not defect to the Rebellion until 1.8 ABY, as per [[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']].</ref> the Alliance launched "[[Operation Cobolt]]," a hit-and-run assault on an [[Imperial orbital base]] over Mantooine. Its twin objectives were to steal an [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]] [[Scandoc/Legends|scandoc]], and then to destroy the base, covering the theft in the process. The core of the mission involved a commando team led by [[Colonel/Legends|Colonels]] [[Anna Seertay/Legends|Anna Seertay]] and [[Toombs]]. These [[Troop/Legends|troops]] were supported by starfighter forces stripped from [[Tierfon/Legends|Tierfon]], [[Homon/Legends|Homon]], [[Farstey]] and the survivors of the [[Tocan system/Legends|Tocan system]] [[Tocan system disaster|defeat]]. The mission was a success although the resistance forces sustained some losses. Shortly after this operation, the Atrivis resistance received a warning from a monitoring station in the neighboring [[Oplovis sector/Legends|Oplovis sector]]. Analyzing Imperial requisition records, [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Zgorth'sth]] was able to predict an attack by [[Fleet Admiral/Legends|Fleet Admiral]] [[Tzenkens]] on Mantooine. With this intelligence, the Rebels sprung their own trap en route, [[Battle of the Generis system|attacking]] the Imperial forces as they left hyperspace in the Generis system with three Alliance [[Cruiser/Legends|cruisers]], defeating the Imperial forces with only minimal casualties.<ref name="RASB" /> In honor of the sector's contribution to the resistance, the Rebel Alliance named a [[Pathfinder-class scout ship|Vangaard Pathfinder]] the ''[[Atrivis Advancer]]'',<ref name="CRO" /> as well as labeling a [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] group the [[Atrivis Day group|''Atrivis Day'']].<ref name="TIE">[[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']]</ref>

===Pentastar Alignment===
====Isolationism====
{{Quote|The New Republic is still merely the Rebellion, thinly disguised as an official entity. They are outlaws, and they will continue to think and do as such. In the Pentastar Alignment, there will be no tolerance for any Rebel insurrection.|Grand Moff Kaine|<ref name="Pentastar" />}}
The conflicts in the Atrivis sector played out against the background of galactic conflict. In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], on the far side of the galaxy from the Atrivis sector, the Empire and the Alliance clashed in an epochal [[Battle of Endor/Legends|battle]] in the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]]. The Alliance proved victorious; in the process, they destroyed the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] and killed the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] himself, leaving the Imperial fleet in disarray.<ref name="Atlas" />

[[File:PentastarAlignment-TEA.jpg|thumb|left|The Pentastar Alignment incorporated the Atrivis sector (bottom right).]]
In response to these developments, Grand Moff Kaine recognized that Imperial authority could quickly crumble across the Outer Rim Territories. He moved swiftly to establish the [[Pentastar Alignment]], an aggregation of fifteen Outer Rim sectors&mdash;including the Atrivis sector at its eastern-most expanse&mdash;that answered to his command from his capital at [[Entralla/Legends|Entralla]].<ref name="Atlas" /> In addition to Kaine as a representative of the Imperial military, the founding [[Pentastar Alignment Treaty]] was signed by Imperial [[Governor/Legends|governor]] [[Ib Dekeet|Dekeet]], [[Commerce Master Commissioner]] [[Gregor Raquoran|Raquoran]] of the [[Velcar Free Commerce Zone]], and corporate representatives [[Wyrn Otro]] and [[Elta Besk]], of [[Galentro Heavy Works]] and [[Dynamic Automata]], respectively.<ref name="Pentastar" />

Kaine, one of the earliest converts to the Emperor's [[New Order/Legends|New Order]],<ref name="Pentastar" /> held strongly to its policy of [[High Human Culture/Legends|Human High Culture]], which he applied throughout his dominion.<ref name="Atlas" /> The powerful corporate entities exploited [[Alien/Legends|alien]] populations across the Alignment, funneling trade and industry profits into Alignment treasuries. With these profits, the Alignment produced a fleet of [[Enforcer-class picket cruiser|''Enforcer''-class picket cruisers]] from its [[Jaemus shipyards|shipyards]] in the [[Obtrexta sector/Legends|Obtrexta sector's]] [[Jaemus system/Legends|Jaemus system]]. These warships formed part of the Alignment navy,<ref name="Pentastar" /> which, spearheaded from the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought]] [[Reaper (Executor-class)|''Reaper'']], was powerful enough to dissuade any challengers. Grand Moff Kaine soon became more feared throughout his realm than the distant Emperor had ever been.<ref name="Atlas" />

As Kaine was not interested in expansionism, and showed little aggression toward sectors outside his direct control, the Alliance, and its successor government, the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], largely left the Alignment alone and instead concentrated on undermining other Imperial warlords.<ref name="Atlas" /> Through until [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]] the Alignment maintained its stranglehold over the Atrivis sector,<ref name="Atlas" /> with the exception of the Republic retaining control of its Outer Rim Communications Center on Generis.<ref name="LC" /> This base was secured with the [[Cracken Flight Group]]<ref name="TLCSB ">''[[The Last Command Sourcebook]]''</ref>&mdash;an elite group of [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|RZ-1 A-wing interceptors]], led by [[Pash Cracken/Legends|Pash Cracken]]'' and composed of pilots that had followed him when he defected from the Empire soon after graduating from the [[Imperial Naval Academy/Legends|Imperial Naval Academy]]<ref name="X-Wing: Wedge's Gamble">''[[X-Wing: Wedge's Gamble]]''</ref>&mdash;except for a short period in [[7 ABY/Legends|7 ABY]], when all of the base's forces were temporarily moved toward the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] in order to cover some of the sectors formerly used by rogue Imperial [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Zsinj]].<ref name="BW">''[[X-Wing: The Bacta War]]''</ref>

====Imperial machinations====
{{Quote|I thought you were out in Atrivis sector, baby-sitting the Outer Rim comm center.''"<br />"''You're behind the times, Generis fell three days ago.|[[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] and Pash Cracken|<ref name="LC" />}}
That year, however, [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] returned from the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] and rallied Imperial forces across the galaxy, including support from the Alignment's military. On the day of 44:8:19, just over four months after his initial strike at [[Obroa-skai/Legends|Obroa-skai]], Thrawn's forces [[Fall of Generis|assaulted]] the Communications Center at Generis.<ref name="Atlas" /> Using a battle plan composed by Thrawn himself, the Imperial forces captured the Communications Center intact&mdash;along with most of the sector fleet supply depots&mdash;despite resistance from an elite Republic [[Squadron/Legends|squadron]] commanded by [[Pash Cracken/Legends|Pash Cracken]].<ref name="LC" />

[[File:Battle_of_Generis.png|thumb|right|The battle of Generis]]
The Republic forces were able to sneak out most of the command staff, however, and deny the Imperials any working ships, but they nevertheless suffered a significant defeat at the hands of Thrawn.<ref name="LC" /> Among the Imperial casualties suffered at this battle was the [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] [[Grodin Tierce]]; [[19 ABY/Legends|ten years]] later, Tierce was impersonated by members of the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] in a bid to take control of that government.<ref name="VF" /> Thrawn's forces later destroyed the Communications Center.<ref name="CSWE" />

From Generis, Thrawn's forces traveled via Fedje to Ketaris, [[Agamar/Legends|Agamar]] and [[Ithor/Legends|Ithor]], all within the space of two days. Thrawn's successes were not to last, however, and on 44:8:27, a mere eight days after his victory at Generis, Thrawn was [[Assassin/Legends|assassinated]] during the [[Battle of Bilbringi (9 ABY)|Battle of Bilbringi]]. With the loss of the genius and charisma of the Grand Admiral, the Empire soon reverted to factionalism, with Kaine maintaining control of the Alignment.<ref name="Atlas" />

The following year, in [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]], a reborn clone of Emperor Palpatine emerged from the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]], drawing together the splintered remains of his former Empire. Kaine was required to support the Emperor, but subsequently died during [[Operation Shadow Hand]]&mdash;a series of military campaigns directed by the Emperor. The Alignment struggled to adjust to the vacuum left by Kaine's death, but remained one of the most significant Imperial governments through into [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]]. The following year, it was incorporated into an Imperial Remnant under the military command of [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]],<ref name="Atlas" /> formerly Grand Admiral Thrawn's second-in-command. Pellaeon remained in control of a large swath of territory, including the Atrivis sector, until [[17 ABY/Legends|17 ABY]], when he suffered a [[Battle of Anx Minor|major defeat]] at [[Anx Minor/Legends|Anx Minor]]. Following this, he retreated to a mere eight sectors in the west of the Alignment, relinquishing control of the Atrivis sector to the New Republic.<ref name="Atlas" />

===New Republic===
{{Quote|Generis has been destroyed by the Yuuzhan Vong, and Esfandia is under attack.|A [[Ryn/Legends|Ryn]] reports on the fate of Generis|<ref name="Heretic III" />}}
The New Republic regained control of Generis and rebuilt the Communications Center.<ref name="CSWE" /> Its role was expanded from the Outer Rim to include the Unknown Regions; at the time, the only such relay center to do so. This made Generis strategically important, but it was never selected for sabotage by the Imperial Remnant, as they considered the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]]&mdash;the dominant power in the Unknown Regions&mdash;to be too isolationist for the Republic to make any successful approaches.<ref name="Heretic III" /> At one point, New Republic agents successfully captured [[Qan Gindoch]] on Mantooine, as part of an operation to disrupt the actions of counterfeiter [[Pendor Gyrr]].<ref name="Wanted">[[Wanted by Cracken (sourcebook)|''Wanted by Cracken'']]</ref>

In [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], the galaxy was invaded by an extra-galactic species known as the [[Yuuzhan Vong]]. They [[Vector Prime|entered]] the galaxy from the far north of the New Territories, and advanced steadily core-ward. One invasion corridor took the Yuuzhan Vong down the Braxant Run, where they assaulted and captured both the [[Attack on the Moltok system|Moltok]] and [[Battle of the Fedje system|Fedje systems]] as they penetrated through the Atrivis sector and beyond. By the [[26 ABY/Legends|following year]], the Yuuzhan Vong were also in control of the Horuz system; however, the Generis system managed to hold out as a lone New Republic stronghold in the region.<ref name="Atlas" />

In [[28 ABY/Legends|28 ABY]], Generis was [[Battle of Generis (Yuuzhan Vong War)|attacked]] and destroyed by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] who were called to the base by an infiltrator armed with a communications [[villip]]. The Yuuzhan Vong then proceeded to [[Battle of Esfandia|attack]] a similar station at [[Esfandia/Legends|Esfandia]] far to the west, the only other communications outpost servicing the Unknown Regions. There, [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] Grand Admiral [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Pellaeon]] defeated the Yuuzhan Vong task force. Subsequently, the center at Generis was restored to operational capacity.<ref name="Heretic III" /> The Yuuzhan Vong War ultimately came to a conclusion in [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]], when the invaders suffered a series of major military defeats.<ref name="Atlas" />

===Under a New Empire===
{{Quote|I am, by right of birth and choice, your true Emperor! Not this Sith usurper, Krayt! It is to me that you all owe your allegiance.|Roan Fel|<ref name="Legacy (2006) 3">[[Legacy (2006) 3|''Legacy'' (2006) 3]]</ref>}}
[[File:Ausdehnung_Galaktisches_Imperium_40_NSY.jpg|thumb|right|upright|The territory of the expanded Galactic Empire encompassed the Atrivis sector.]]
Within the space of [[40 ABY/Legends|eleven years]], the Atrivis sector was reclaimed by a resurgent [[Fel Empire|Empire]], which had expanded its borders to the edge of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] and beyond. This new Empire slowly absorbed much of the galaxy through peaceful means, before launching, in [[127 ABY]], the [[Sith–Imperial War]] against the other major political power, the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]]. By the close of this conflict in [[130 ABY]], the Empire had gained control of the rest of the galaxy; however, division existed within the Empire. By [[137 ABY]], the Atrivis sector had become part of a [[Empire-in-exile|large portion]] of the New Territories that supported [[Roan Fel]], the deposed former Emperor who had been betrayed at the conclusion of the Sith–Imperial War by his [[One Sith|Sith]] allies.<ref name="Atlas" />

==Inhabitants==
===Native species===
====Dazouri====
[[File:Dazouri.jpg|thumb|right|150px|A Dazouri]]
{{Main|Dazouri}}
The Dazouri were a species of polymorphs native to Gibbela.<ref name="Hiding" /> These beings were diminutive while in their settled form, however, when angered, they transformed into vicious predators double their original size.<ref name="CSWEGibbela">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> In this form, they had sharps claws capable of rending flesh and severing limbs. This was discovered by an Imperial scouting team to its detriment. The Dazouri were farmers, living in primitive cloth dwellings.<ref name="Tales" /> At least one Dazouri, Boss [[Kaggle]], ventured offworld. He became a minor [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] in the [[Elrood sector/Legends|Elrood sector]].<ref name="Planets3">''[[Planets of the Galaxy, Volume Three]]''</ref>

====Ho'Din====
{{Main|Ho'Din/Legends}}
[[File:IwoKulka.jpg|thumb|right|150px|A Ho'Din]]
The Ho'Din were one of two sentient species native to Moltok, and were the most prominent of the species indigenous to the Atrivis sector. They were a tall reptilian species, with dark eyes, lipless mouths and distinctive [[Snake/Legends|snake]]-like hair. After industrialization almost ruined their world, the Ho'Din focused on organic technology, living in tree villages and structures literally grown from plants. This approach was inspired by their religion, [[Dinante Fli'R]], whose tenets required them to be respectful to plants. Ho'Din were widely regarded throughout the galaxy as master botanists and healers. Notable Ho'Din healers included [[Baji]]<ref name="Lost">''[[The Lost City of the Jedi]]''</ref> and [[Ism Oolos]].<ref name="Planet">''[[Planet of Twilight]]''</ref> Ho'Din Jedi included [[Iwo Kulka]]<ref name="Vader">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref> and [[Plett]].<ref name="CoJ" /> The Ho'Din established colony worlds in neighboring sectors, such as [[Anemcoro]]<ref name="No Disintegrations West End Games">[[No Disintegrations (West End Games)|''No Disintegrations'']]</ref> in the Albarrio sector.<ref name="TEAOC" />

====Makurth====
{{Main|Makurth/Legends}}
[[File:Makurth-square.jpg|thumb|right|150px|A Makurth]]
The Makurth were the second sentient species on Moltok. They were saurians covered in green scales with four horns on their heads.<ref name="Bane" /> They were nocturnal carnivores, known for their terrifying scream. A number of Makurth found employment as bodyguards with the criminal organization [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]].<ref name="CCG" /> One notable Makurth was Fohargh, who trained with the Brotherhood of Darkness during the [[New Sith Wars|Light and Darkness War]].<ref name="Bane" />

====Zeffliffl====
{{Main|Zeffliffl (species)|l1=Zeffliffl}}
The Zeffliffl were a species from the world Zeffliffl, the fourth planet of [[Markbee's Star]], and appeared to be multi-humped stacks of dark green [[Seaweed/Legends|seaweed]]. The leaf-like beings lived in shallow seas, and when traveling offworld, they periodically sprayed themselves with [[salt water]] to keep themselves hydrated. Their language sounded like leaves swirled through water. A group of the species traveled to [[Crseih Station]] to seek healing from the [[Waru]]. There, he successfully healed their ailing member.<ref name="CS" />

===Immigrated species===
Beyond its indigenous inhabitants, many exotic species called the Atrivis sector home. Around [[30,000 BBY]], the Rakata utilized [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-based [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrives]] to unite widely spread worlds into the Rakatan [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]]. One such world was Generis,<ref name="Atlas" /> where they constructed large temples.<ref name="TLCSB " /> However, after five thousand years of galactic dominance, plague caused the collapse of the Infinite Empire,<ref name="Atlas" /> and the species later became extinct. Their temples collapsed into ruins overtaken by the jungle, leaving no clues for later settlers as to how or why they died out.<ref name="TLCSB " />

[[File:Despayre.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Alien convicts worked on Despayre.]]
During the administration of the Republic, Humans occupied many of the Atrivis sector worlds, including Mantooine, Fest, Iridium and Atrivis 7. Some notable Human inhabitants of the Atrivis sector included Travia Chan, the Alliance [[Commander-in-Chief/Legends|Commander-in-Chief]] for the sector. One of the original founders of the Fest Resistance Group,<ref name="RASB" /> she continued working at the Generis base until its conquest in 9 ABY.<ref name="LC" /> Chan's [[Chief of Staff/Legends|Chief of Staff]] was [[Loom Carplin]], a survivor of the original Mantooine cell.<ref name="RASB" /> Also from Mantooine was the Human [[Brandei]]. Rather than joining the resistance movement, he rose to a high rank in the Empire, commanding the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Judicator/Legends|''Judicator'']].<ref name="LC" /> Sullustan colonists also settled in the sector on the planet Hethar.<ref name="CotG" />

A diverse group of species passed through the sector as tourists aboard the ''Kuari Princess'', a luxury liner that traveled the Relgim Run through [[Maelstrom Nebula/Legends|The Maelstrom]].<ref name="SWAJ" /> Many aliens were also brought to the sector and imprisoned on the planet Despayre, and later used as slave labor in constructing the first Death Star. These included [[Brigian]]s, [[Cerean/Legends|Cereans]], [[Givin/Legends|Givin]], [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]], [[Pho Ph'eahian]]s, [[Mirialan/Legends|Mirialans]], Wookiees, [[Ugnaught/Legends|Ugnaughts]], [[Zelosian]]s,<ref name="DS" /> [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'leks]],<ref name="Lethal" /> and [[Ithorian/Legends|Ithorians]].<ref name="DSTC" /> Various individuals were also forcibly transported to the Gree Baaker Labor Camp<ref name="Target" /> and to Desolation Station.<ref name="Elite" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[Paul Murphy]] created the Atrivis sector for the [[West End Games]] sourcebook, ''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]'', first published in [[1990]]. Murphy used the sector to illustrate possible structures for sector resistance groups. This publication placed three planets&mdash;Fest, Generis and Mantooine&mdash;in the sector and provided a number of anecdotal stories relating its struggles against the Galactic Empire.<ref name="RASB" /> The sector was also mentioned in a number of other West End Games' products, but given little expansion at that time.<ref name="TLCSB " /><ref name="DES">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref>

The short story [[A Certain Point of View (short story)|''A Certain Point of View'']], written by [[Charlene Newcomb]] and published in [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 8|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 8]], mentioned the "'''Generis sector'''."<ref name="SWAJ" /> Given the prior placement of Generis in the Atrivis sector, and no further mention of a Generis sector, this is interpreted as an alternative name for the same sector. The novel, [[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']], written by [[Barbara Hambly]] and published is [[1995]], mentioned the [[Atravis sector/Legends|Atravis sector]]. While it is possible this was originally a misspelling of this sector, subsequent sources such as the ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' treated it as a distinct entity.<ref name="SWE" /><ref>
{{JCFCite|url=posts/28605679|board=Literature|thread=The Essential Atlas and Galactic Cartography: Official Discussion|user=[[Jason Fry|jasonfry]]|date=2008-06-18|time=1:58 PM|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200802094502/https://boards.theforce.net/threads/the-essential-atlas-and-galactic-cartography-official-discussion.21938930/page-56}}</ref>
<imagemap>
File:AtrivisSector-SWR.png|thumb|right|231px|The Atrivis sector map created for ''Star Wars: Rebellion'' containing three worlds subsequently removed from the sector.
circle 113 221 20 [[Despayre]]
circle 190 164 20 [[Generis/Legends|Generis]]
circle 191 50 20 [[Fedje]]
circle 53 133 20 [[Moltok/Legends|Moltok]]
circle 62 288 20 [[Nam'ta]]
circle 143 107 20 [[Spefik]]
circle 104 51 20 [[Tibrin/Legends|Tibrin]]
circle 28 208 20 [[Togoria/Legends|Togoria]]
circle 134 295 20 [[Trammis III/Legends|Trammis III]]
circle 43 26 20 [[Zeffliffl]]

desc bottom-left
</imagemap>
The Atrivis sector was one of the many sectors included in the computer game, [[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']], released in [[1998]]. ''Rebellion'' placed ten planets in the sector; an additional nine from those previously established. However, ''Rebellion'' contradicted numerous sources in some of its placements. As such, [[Leland Chee]], [[Holocron continuity database|Keeper of the Holocron]], has stated that when ''Rebellion''{{'s}} placements conflict with other existing [[canon]] placements, ''Rebellion'' is overridden.<ref name="Tasty">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=118855&start=15#3897382|thread=Galaxy Map Discussion|user=[[Leland Chee|Tasty Taste]]|date=2003-05-01|time=1:40 PM|quote=Things that do not contradict established continuity can be considered canon, including any locations developed specifically for game.}}</ref> In the case of the Atrivis sector, this applies to three worlds, [[Tibrin/Legends|Tibrin]], [[Togoria/Legends|Togoria]], and [[Trammis III/Legends|Trammis III]]. Tibrin and Togoria have been placed in the Mid Rim,<ref name="UAA">''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]''</ref> while Trammis III has been placed in the [[Centrality/Legends|Centrality]].<ref name="GMR5">{{GamerCite|5|A Campaign Guide to the Centrality}}</ref> This left six new planets receiving placements in this sector: Nam'ta, Despayre, Moltok, Spefik, Fedje and Zeffliffl. In its internal encyclopedia, ''Rebellion'' also misspelled the sector name on a couple of occasion, spelling it as both "'''Artivis'''" and "'''Artivas'''."<ref name="SWR" />

The next significant mention of the Atrivis sector occurred in an article on the [[HoloNet News (original website)|HoloNet News]] website, published in [[2002]], which detailed a Republic strike against pirates operating in the sector. This article placed Vuchelle in the sector, as well as implying a connection with the planet Iridium.<ref name="Hnn" /> The sector received another mention on the HoloNetNews website,<ref name="HNN50">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|50|news/1344_1.html|Senator Moe Killed in Blast}}</ref> as well as in the Clone Wars-era novel, ''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]'', written by [[Karen Traviss]] and published in [[2006]].<ref name="Republic Commando" /> Further planets were not added to the sector until the release of the seminal work, ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', co-written by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]] and published in [[2009]]. This publication included a map of the Atrivis sector, which confirmed Iridium's location, as well as adding Devon, Gibbela and Hethar to the sector. The ''Atlas'' also significantly expanded available information on the sector, providing details on its location, exploration, population density, and political history, including its incorporation into the Pentastar Alignment,<ref name="Atlas" /> a reference back to material originally published by West End Games in [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 3|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 3]] in [[1994]].<ref name="Pentastar" />

Following the publication of the ''Atlas'', [[StarWars.com]] published an [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|Online Companion]]. Its first update included an appendix that included sector placements for many star systems; information that was not included in the original publication. This appendix placed Gree Baaker and Shar'Ack in the Atrivis sector. Additional updates to the Online Companion included a sector map of the Outer Rim Territories, which revealed the patchwork of sectors the Atrivis sector was part of, and, later, the addition of newly published or previously omitted systems to the appendix. The [[June 1]], [[2010]] update placed Desolation Station within the sector, incorporating several events from ''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Elite Squadron]]'' into the sector's history.<ref name="TEAOC" />
